L78@P2: PRINCIPLE 1 | No Student or Educator Data for Training — Ever, With
L79@P2: One Narrow Safety Exception
L80@P2: • "Academy" means the signing institution, including its students, educators, staff, and
L81@P2: administrators.
L82@P2: • "Breach" means any unauthorized access to, disclosure of, alteration of, or destruction
L83@P2: of Covered Data.
L84@P2: • "Zero Data Retention (ZDR)" means that inputs (prompts) and outputs (responses) are
L85@P2: not stored, logged, or retained beyond the immediate session required to deliver the
L86@P2: service.
L87@P2: • "Synthetic Data" means data that is artificially generated to simulate patterns, scenarios,
L88@P2: or edge cases. Under this agreement, Synthetic Data may be used only if it is not
L89@P2: created from, seeded with, tuned on, or reasonably reversible to Covered Data.
L90@P2: • "Agentic or Action-Taking Feature" means any AI capability that can initiate, approve,
L91@P2: transmit, modify, or execute actions on behalf of a user, online or offline, rather than only
L92@P2: generating informational output.
L93@P2: • "Memory Files" means anything an AI Provider Educational Product saves about a user
L94@P2: between sessions, stored facts, preferences, profiles, or conversation summaries, so it
L95@P2: can "remember" them later. All Memory Files are Covered Data under this agreement.
L96@P2: PART I — THE TEN CORE PRINCIPLES
L97@P2: Each principle below is a binding commitment. The AI Provider must comply with all ten, across
L98@P2: every AI Provider Educational Product it provides to an EDU Customer who has opted in to the
L99@P2: principles. Complying with some principles but not others is not compliance.
L100@P2: These principles are effective from the date signed and remain in force for a term of two years
L101@P2: (the “Effective Date”). To continue past that term, the agreement must be renewed in writing by
L102@P2: both the Academy and the AI Provider every two years. The Academy may terminate the AI
L103@P2: Provider's participation in the Standard immediately upon any material breach by the AI
L104@P2: Provider that is not cured within the period set forth in Principle 5.
L105@P2: Compliance with Applicable Laws
L106@P2: All aspects of this Standard shall be implemented in accordance with all applicable federal,
L107@P2: state, and local laws and regulations, including FERPA, COPPA, IDEA, and applicable student
L108@P2: privacy, data protection, accessibility, civil rights, consumer protection, and education laws.
L109@P2: Nothing in this Standard limits any right, protection, or obligation provided by law. Where this
L110@P2: Standard provides stronger protections, those stronger protections shall apply to the extent
L111@P2: permitted by law.

L173@P4: Annual Confirmation Required:
L174@P4: Upon request, the AI Provider must deliver a written annual statement, in plain language, signed
L175@P4: by a senior officer to the Academy, confirming that (1) no Covered Data was used for training
L176@P4: outside the Narrow Safety Exception in the preceding twelve months, and (2) no data, learnings,
L177@P4: or model improvements derived from Covered Data crossed from safety systems into any other
L178@P4: model or product.

L209@P5: • Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) Required, Including New Features:
L210@P5: Before any material new feature, capability, or data collection practice is activated for an AI
L211@P5: Provider Educational Product, the AI Provider must complete a Privacy Impact Assessment
L212@P5: (PIA) in accordance with its standard practices. For purposes of this requirement, a change is
L213@P5: “material” if it is reasonably likely to increase student privacy or safety risk, including through the
L214@P5: collection or use of new categories of data or new purposes for existing data, biometrics,

L216@P5: safety functionality, or other changes reasonably likely to increase such risk. Upon request, and

L228@P5: • Provide the EDU Customer with the ability to export all Customer Content and other

L230@P5: machine-readable formats (such as JSON, CSV, or PDF). Any category of Covered Data

L34@P1: Abstract
L35@P1: How are new college graduates affected by the rise of artificial intelligence, and what can this tell
L36@P1: us about the mechanisms behind AI's overall labor market effects? We use administrative records
L37@P1: on college graduates to observe how economic outcomes among college majors with differing
L38@P1: levels of labor market AI exposure have evolved since large language models became available.
L39@P1: We find that post-graduation employment, earnings, and job switching patterns among the most
L40@P1: AI-exposed college majors began to diverge immediately following the introduction of ChatGPT
L41@P1: in late 2022. In regression-adjusted estimates, the most AI-exposed decile of college majors saw
L42@P1: their likelihood of initial employment decline by five percentage points, while full-quarter initial
L43@P1: earnings declined by thirteen percent. This earnings decline is comparable in magnitude to the
L44@P1: earnings losses associated with graduating into a large recession. Roughly half of the decline in
L45@P1: earnings is attributable to lower earnings within the industry sectors that employ these
L46@P1: graduates, with the remainder resulting from a shift in the industry mix into lower-wage sectors
L47@P1: such as restaurants and retail. The effects attenuate as graduates move further from labor
L48@P1: market entry but remain substantial for the most exposed majors.
